# Sim racing on SteamOS: compatibility guide

Which racing sims run on SteamOS (Steam Machine, Steam Deck, desktop Linux), how to set them up, what breaks, and what telemetry Pitwall can read. Every known issue links its source.

The Pitwall app shows the same entries plus **live** ratings from Valve (Steam Deck compatibility), ProtonDB and Are We Anti-Cheat Yet, refreshed daily.

## BeamNG.drive

**Status:** ✅ Works  
**Runs via:** Native Linux  
**Steam:** [284160](https://store.steampowered.com/app/284160) · [ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com/app/284160)

### Setup

1. Install from Steam. On SteamOS the native Linux version is the default; leave 'Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool' off.
2. In game: Options > Other > Protocols. Enable OutGauge (IP 127.0.0.1, port 4444) and MotionSim (IP 127.0.0.1, port 4445).
3. Drive to a start/finish point and press 'Set start line' in Pitwall to time laps.

### In-game force feedback

1. Options > Controls > find your wheel > the steering binding > Force Feedback.
2. Raise Strength until the wheel feels weighty but big and small forces still feel different.
3. Then lower Smoothing gradually for more detail; raise it a little again if rattling starts.

Community starting points: Smoothing around 150, Steering lock strength 75-100%, Side acceleration 0% on roads or around 10% on track, Reduce strength while parked on.

Sources: <https://docs.beamng.com/support/hardware/steering_wheel_setup/>, <https://briankoponen.com/beamng-drive-logitech-g29-g920-settings>

**Wheel rotation:** 900°. BeamNG adapts steering per car; keep the base at 900° and match it in Options > Controls > the wheel's FFB/steering settings.

### Performance

- Dynamic reflections, shadow quality and the number of AI/traffic vehicles have the biggest impact on frame rate.

### Known issues

- The native version is Vulkan-only and needs a fully featured Vulkan driver. ([source](https://documentation.beamng.com/support/troubleshooting/steamdeck_linux/))
- HDR may be broken or unreliable under SteamOS Gaming Mode (Gamescope). ([source](https://beamng.com/goto/post?id=1465767))
- Native and Proton versions use different user folders, so settings and mods can seem to vanish after switching. Native folder: ~/.local/share/BeamNG/BeamNG.drive/current. ([source](https://documentation.beamng.com/support/troubleshooting/steamdeck_linux/))
- Can use more than 16 GB of memory; without enough RAM and swap the game may close. ([source](https://documentation.beamng.com/support/troubleshooting/steamdeck_linux/))
- Community report (MOZA R5): force feedback felt flatter on the native version than under Proton. If FFB feels weak, try forcing Proton as a comparison. ([source](https://www.beamng.com/posts/1787800/))

## Assetto Corsa

**Status:** 🛠️ Works with setup  
**Runs via:** Proton  
**Steam:** [244210](https://store.steampowered.com/app/244210) · [ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com/app/244210)

### Setup

1. Install from Steam; it runs under Proton.
2. For telemetry, Pitwall can set up the winecarte bridge for you: Game guide → this game → Set up telemetry bridge. It downloads winecarte and adds it to the game's launch options; restart the game afterwards.
3. Pitwall shows the bridge as running once /dev/shm/acpmf_physics appears.

> Pitwall can set up the telemetry bridge for you: Game guide → this game → **Set up telemetry bridge**.

Bridges: [simshmbridge](https://github.com/Spacefreak18/simshmbridge), [winecarte](https://github.com/srounce/winecarte)

### In-game force feedback

1. Content Manager > Settings > Controls > Force Feedback (or Options > Controls in the AC launcher).

MOZA's recommendation: Gain 60-90% depending on car, Filter 0%, Minimum force 0%, Kerb 15%, Road 15%, Slip 10%, ABS 0%.

Sources: <https://eu.mozaracing.com/blogs/blog/moza-settings-guide-for-assetto-corsa>

### Known issues

- Shared memory stays inside the Wine prefix unless a bridge runs in the same prefix as the game. ([source](https://github.com/srounce/winecarte))
- Content Manager and Custom Shaders Patch need extra setup under Proton; check recent ProtonDB reports for the current method. ([source](https://www.protondb.com/app/244210))

## Automobilista 2

**Status:** 🛠️ Works with setup  
**Runs via:** Proton  
**Steam:** [1066890](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1066890) · [ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com/app/1066890)

### Setup

1. Install from Steam; runs under Proton.
2. For telemetry: Game guide → this game → Set up telemetry bridge (winecarte), then restart the game.
3. In AMS2's options, make sure Shared Memory is set to 'Project CARS 2'.

> Pitwall can set up the telemetry bridge for you: Game guide → this game → **Set up telemetry bridge**.

Bridges: [winecarte](https://github.com/srounce/winecarte)

### Known issues

- Force feedback has been lost with some Proton versions (reported with a Logitech G29); one user restored it with GE-Proton 7-44 but lost it again after alt-tabbing. ([source](https://forum.reizastudios.com/threads/linux-and-ffb.36382/))
- Avoid re-plugging the wheel while the game is running; it can break controller mappings. ([source](https://www.protondb.com/app/1066890))

## rFactor 2

**Status:** 🛠️ Works with setup  
**Runs via:** Proton  
**Steam:** [365960](https://store.steampowered.com/app/365960) · [ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com/app/365960)

### Setup

1. Install from Steam; runs under Proton.
2. Install the rF2 Shared Memory Map plugin (Windows version) into the game's Plugins folder and enable it in the game's settings.
3. Then: Game guide → this game → Set up telemetry bridge (winecarte), and restart the game.

> Pitwall can set up the telemetry bridge for you: Game guide → this game → **Set up telemetry bridge**.

Bridges: [winecarte](https://github.com/srounce/winecarte), [rF2SharedMemoryMapPlugin](https://github.com/TheIronWolfModding/rF2SharedMemoryMapPlugin)

### Known issues

- Community reports say it runs; check ProtonDB for the current recommended Proton version. ([source](https://www.protondb.com/app/365960))
- Don't use the Wine-specific build of rF2SharedMemoryMapPlugin together with winecarte; both write the same files. Use the normal Windows plugin. ([source](https://github.com/srounce/winecarte))

## Le Mans Ultimate

**Status:** ⚠️ Community fixes only  
**Runs via:** Proton  
**Steam:** [2399420](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2399420) · [ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com/app/2399420)

### Setup

1. The developer lists Linux and Steam Deck as unsupported.
2. Community reports use a custom Proton build (GE-Proton10-4-LMU). Expect tinkering.
3. For telemetry: Game guide → this game → Set up telemetry bridge (winecarte). LMU's built-in shared memory (LMU_Data) is read directly.

> Pitwall can set up the telemetry bridge for you: Game guide → this game → **Set up telemetry bridge**.

Bridges: [winecarte](https://github.com/srounce/winecarte)

### Known issues

- Developer: 'MacOS, Linux and Steamdeck is unsupported at this time.' ([source](https://lemansultimate.com/?p=1543))
- For menu lag, community reports suggest changing 'CEF mode' in UserData/player/Settings.JSON. ([source](https://www.protondb.com/app/2399420))

## RaceRoom Racing Experience

**Status:** 🛠️ Works with setup  
**Runs via:** Proton  
**Steam:** [211500](https://store.steampowered.com/app/211500) · [ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com/app/211500)

### Setup

1. Install from Steam; runs under Proton.
2. Telemetry: Pitwall reads RaceRoom's $R3E shared memory, but it needs a bridge that mirrors it into /dev/shm. winecarte doesn't list RaceRoom yet, so this is for advanced users for now.

### Known issues

- Community report: force feedback didn't work with a Logitech G29 even though the wheel worked in other games. ([source](https://www.protondb.com/app/211500))

## DiRT Rally 2.0

**Status:** ✅ Works  
**Runs via:** Proton  
**Steam:** [690790](https://store.steampowered.com/app/690790) · [ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com/app/690790)

### Setup

1. Install from Steam; runs under Proton.
2. Pitwall can switch on telemetry for you: it edits hardware_settings_config.xml in the game's Proton prefix to enable UDP (extradata 3, port 20777). Run the game once first so the file exists.

> Pitwall can do the telemetry step for you: Game guide → this game → **Do this for me**.

## Live for Speed

**Status:** ✅ Works  
**Runs via:** Proton

### Setup

1. Not on Steam: download from lfs.net and add it to Steam as a non-Steam game with Proton.
2. In LFS's cfg.txt set: OutGauge Mode 1, OutGauge IP 127.0.0.1, OutGauge Port 4444.

### Known issues

- BeamNG's OutGauge uses the Live for Speed format, so the same Pitwall adapter reads both. ([source](https://docs.beamng.com/modding/protocols/))

## iRacing

**Status:** ⚠️ Community fixes only  
**Runs via:** Proton  
**Steam:** [266410](https://store.steampowered.com/app/266410) · [ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com/app/266410)

### Setup

1. Runs under Proton, but only offline Test Drive works: online racing needs iRacing to enable its anti-cheat (EOS) for Linux.
2. Show support in iRacing's 'iRacing should support Linux' forum thread.

### Known issues

- EOS is not enabled for Linux, so multiplayer doesn't work; only Test Drive. ([source](https://www.protondb.com/app/266410))
- Listed as Broken (Easy Anti-Cheat) on Are We Anti-Cheat Yet. ([source](https://areweanticheatyet.com))

## Where this information comes from

- **[Steam Deck compatibility (Valve)](https://store.steampowered.com)**: Valve's own testing; official but only covers what Valve tested.
- **[ProtonDB](https://www.protondb.com)**: Crowd-sourced reports with Proton versions, launch options and tinkering steps.
- **[Are We Anti-Cheat Yet](https://areweanticheatyet.com)**: Tracks whether anti-cheat allows Linux; the deciding factor for online sims.
- **[GamingOnLinux anti-cheat list](https://www.gamingonlinux.com/anticheat/)**: Second source for anti-cheat status, with news on changes.
- **[awesome-linux-simracing](https://github.com/LukasLichten/awesome-linux-simracing)**: Community index of Linux sim racing tools, drivers and bridges.

Spotted something out of date? [Open a game report](../../../issues/new?template=game_report.yml).
